etymologies.heading: Etymology 1
paragraphs: Probably from Italian antico (“ancient”), used to describe ancient wall paintings from classical times, from Latin antiquus (“venerable”). See also Italian grottesco (“grotesque”). Doublet of antique.
senses: (architecture, art, obsolete) A grotesque representation of a figure; a gargoyle.
(obsolete) To make a fool of, to cause to look ridiculous.

etymologies.heading: Etymology 2
senses: (animation) A pose, often exaggerated, in anticipation of an action; for example, a brief squat before jumping
